Show that the relation R on the set Z of integers, given by R = {(a, b) : 5 divides (a − b)}, is an equivalence relation.

Bag I contains 4 red and 2 black balls, and Bag II contains 3 red and 5 black balls. One bag is chosen at random and a ball is drawn from it. The ball is found to be red. Find the probability that it was drawn from Bag II.

2x + y − z = 1

Using integration, find the area of the region bounded by the parabola y² = 4x and the line x = 3.
OR
Using integration, find the area of the region enclosed by the ellipse x²/16 + y²/9 = 1.

Maximise Z = 3x + 2y

A craft teacher gives each student a square sheet of cardboard of side 24 cm. An open box is to be made by cutting a square of side x cm from each corner and folding up the flaps. The teacher asks the students to make the box that can hold the maximum volume.
(a) Express the volume V of the box in terms of x.
(b) Find dV/dx.
(c) Find the value of x for which the volume is maximum, and find the maximum volume.
OR
(c) Find the values of x for which dV/dx = 0 and explain why one of them cannot be the side of the square that is cut off.

A factory has two machines, A and B. Machine A produces 60% of the items and machine B produces the remaining 40%. It is found that 2% of the items produced by machine A and 1% of the items produced by machine B are defective. An item is picked at random from the day's production.
(a) Find the probability that the item was produced by machine A and is defective.
(b) Find the probability that the item is defective.
(c) If the item is found to be defective, find the probability that it was produced by machine A.
OR
(c) If the item is found to be defective, find the probability that it was produced by machine B.

A bookshop sells Physics, Chemistry and Mathematics guide books. On Monday it sold 10, 8 and 12 copies of the three books respectively, and on Tuesday it sold 6, 10 and 9 copies. The selling prices of the three books are ₹300, ₹250 and ₹400 per copy respectively.
(a) Write the sales of the two days as a matrix with one row for each day, and state its order.
(b) Using matrix multiplication, find the amount collected on Monday.
(c) Find the total amount collected on the two days together.
OR
(c) If the price of each book is increased by 10%, find the amount that would have been collected on Monday.

OR

A carpenter makes chairs and tables. Each chair needs 1 hour on the cutting machine and 2 hours on the polishing machine, while each table needs 1 hour on the cutting machine and 1 hour on the polishing machine. The cutting machine is available for at most 8 hours a day and the polishing machine for at most 12 hours a day. The profit is ₹400 on a chair and ₹300 on a table. Formulate this as a linear programming problem and solve it graphically to find how many chairs and tables should be made each day to get the maximum profit.
OR
Solve the following linear programming problem graphically:
Minimise Z = 2x + 3y
subject to the constraints x + 2y ≥ 6, 3x + y ≥ 8, x ≥ 0, y ≥ 0.

A farmer has 200 m of fencing wire. He wants to fence a rectangular field that lies along a straight river. No fence is needed along the river bank, so the wire is used only for the other three sides. Let x metres be the length of each of the two sides perpendicular to the river.
(a) Express the area A of the field as a function of x.
(b) Find dA/dx and the value of x at which dA/dx = 0.
(c) Find the maximum area that can be enclosed and the dimensions of the field.
OR
(c) Use the second derivative test to show that the area found is a maximum.

In a school, 60% of the students play cricket, 40% play football and 25% play both games. A student is selected at random.
(a) Find the probability that the student plays football, given that the student plays cricket.
(b) Find the probability that the student plays neither game.
(c) Are the events 'plays cricket' and 'plays football' independent? Justify your answer.
OR
(c) Find the probability that the student plays cricket, given that the student does not play football.

(a) Find the distance OA.
(b) Find the vector AB and the distance AB.
(c) Find the cosine of the angle between OA and AB.
OR
(c) Find the projection of the vector AB on the vector OA.

OR

For a quiz contest, nine teams are given the numbers 1 to 9. The organiser forms the set A = {1, 2, 3, 4, 5, 6, 7, 8, 9} and wants to seat teams together in groups using the relation R on A defined by R = {(a, b) : |a − b| is even}.
(a) Show that R is reflexive and symmetric.
(b) Show that R is transitive.
(c) Write the equivalence classes [1] and [2].
OR
(c) The function f : A → A is defined by f(x) = 10 − x. Show that f is both one-one and onto.

In a laboratory, a culture of bacteria grows at a rate proportional to the number of bacteria present, so that dN/dt = kN, where N is the number of bacteria at time t hours and k is a positive constant. At the start there were 1000 bacteria, and the number doubled in 2 hours.
(a) Write the order and the degree of the differential equation dN/dt = kN.
(b) Solve the differential equation to find N in terms of t and k.
(c) Find the number of bacteria present after 6 hours.
OR
(c) After how many hours will there be 16000 bacteria?

A handicraft unit makes baskets and mats. Each basket needs 2 hours of weaving and 1 hour of finishing, while each mat needs 1 hour of weaving and 2 hours of finishing. Each day at most 20 hours of weaving and 16 hours of finishing are available. The profit is ₹40 on a basket and ₹30 on a mat. Let x baskets and y mats be made in a day.
(a) Write the constraints of this linear programming problem.
(b) Find the corner points of the feasible region.
(c) How many baskets and mats should be made each day to earn the maximum profit? Find the maximum profit.
OR
(c) If the profit on a mat rises to ₹60 (with ₹40 on a basket), find the new maximum profit.
